title: An 18-month-old's messy try with a spoon is the milestone
summary: CDC lists trying a spoon at 18 months, an attempt rather than neat independent eating.
body: The verb CDC chose for the 18-month spoon line is tries. The child attempts the utensil. A tip on the same page says learning to eat and drink is messy but fun, so a clumsy attempt matches the page. That attempt is the whole item. It is earlier and weaker than a second-birthday line that says the child eats with a spoon. CDC includes a behavior when at least three out of four children show it by the age on the page. If the try has not appeared, the page wants a conversation with the child's clinician and, where needed, a real screening tool. The checklist alone does not diagnose anyone.

sources.title: Milestones by 18 Months

sources.note: Supports the tries-to-use-a-spoon milestone. Public-domain CDC page. Paraphrased.
